entries.name: Adobe Photoshop

engines.name: Layer style effects
engines.does: Non-destructive per-layer effects (shadows, glows, bevel, overlays, stroke) stored as editable parameters on the layer.

engines.name: Smart Objects and Smart Filters
engines.does: Containers that keep the source pixels or vector data and re-apply transforms and filters from stored settings.

engines.name: Neural Filters (Sensei)
engines.does: Machine-learning filter workspace for portrait, colour and depth edits, split into released, beta and waitlist filters.

engines.name: Generative Fill (Firefly and partner models)
engines.does: Prompt-driven fill of a selection by a model chosen in the Contextual Task Bar.

capabilities.does: Sets how a layer or paint stroke combines with pixels below. Modes are grouped as Normal, Darken, Lighten, Contrast and Comparative, each with a defined per-channel rule such as multiply, screen or difference.
capabilities.inputs: layer or tool plus mode choice

capabilities.does: Ten effects can be stacked on any layer: bevel and emboss, stroke, inner and outer glow, inner and drop shadow, satin, and colour, gradient and pattern overlays. Parameters include angle, altitude, size, spread, choke, contour and noise.

Adjustment layers store Levels, Curves, Hue/Saturation, Black and White, Brightness/Contrast, Color Balance or Selective Color settings and apply them to everything below. Fill layers add solid, gradient or pattern content without changing layers beneath.
capabilities.outputs: tonally changed composite, original pixels intact

capabilities.does: A Smart Object keeps the original image or vector data inside the layer, so scaling, warping and filters can be redone from the source. It can be embedded or linked to an external file that updates every copy.
Filters applied to a Smart Object appear as separate entries that can be reordered, hidden, re-edited or masked. Some filters, such as Lens Blur and Vanishing Point, are not available in this mode.

A pixel mask on a layer or group hides or reveals content by grey level. It can be built from a selection (reveal or hide), from layer transparency, or copied between layers by dragging the thumbnail.
capabilities.inputs: layer plus selection or painted greyscale

capabilities.does: Selection tools include rectangular, elliptical, single-row and single-column marquees, freehand, polygonal and magnetic lassos, Quick Selection, Magic Wand and Object Selection. A moving border marks the active area that limits edits.
capabilities.inputs: pointer drag or click on image

capabilities.does: Refine Selection and Mask offers view modes (onion skin, marching ants, overlay, on black, on white, black and white, on layers) and two refine algorithms: Color Aware for simple backgrounds, Object Aware for hair and complex edges.

Brush Settings panel groups shape, texture, dual brush, scattering and colour options. Shape dynamics vary size, angle and roundness by jitter percent and by control sources: fade, pen pressure, tilt, stylus wheel, rotation, direction.
capabilities.inputs: brush tip, dynamics values, pen input

capabilities.does: Colour dynamics change hue, saturation or brightness during a stroke. The Apply Per Tip switch decides whether variation happens at every stamp or only once at the start of each stroke.

Fills a selection from sampled surroundings. Settings: sampling area (auto, rectangular, custom brush), colour adaptation, rotation adaptation, scale, mirror, sample all layers, and output to current, new or duplicate layer.

Smart Sharpen has Amount, Radius and Reduce Noise controls and a Remove choice of Gaussian Blur (like Unsharp Mask), Lens Blur (edge-aware, fewer halos) or Motion Blur. Running it on a Smart Object keeps it editable.
capabilities.inputs: pixel layer, three sliders, blur type

capabilities.does: Lens Blur takes a depth map from none, transparency or a layer mask, a blur focal distance, an iris shape with radius, blade curvature and rotation, specular highlight brightness and threshold, and noise amount with uniform or Gaussian distribution.

Color Range selects by skin tones (optionally with face detection), sampled colours (with localized clusters, fuzziness and invert), a preset colour or tonal range, or out-of-gamut colours. Preview shows the selection in black and white or the image.
Retouch tools: Spot Healing Brush, Healing Brush, Patch, Red Eye, Eraser (including history-based erasing), Background and Magic Erasers, Blur, Sharpen, Smudge, Dodge, Burn and Sponge.
The Liquify dialog pushes pixels with brush tools: Forward Warp, Pucker, Bloat and Twirl, with brush size and pressure. Used on a Smart Object, the distortion stays editable.

The Pen tool draws Bezier paths in three modes: shape layer with vector mask, work path, or filled pixels. Corner points come from clicking, smooth points from dragging handles. Options include auto add/delete and rubber-band preview.

The Crop tool takes ratio presets (1:1, 4:5, 5:7, 2:3, 16:9, original, width by height by resolution), can keep or delete cropped pixels, offers a classic mode, a crop shield overlay and a custom preset list.

A filter workspace driven by machine-learning models for portrait edits (expression, age, gaze), colourisation, style transfer and depth or lighting effects. Filters are listed as featured, beta or waitlist.
capabilities.outputs: filtered layer or new output layer

capabilities.does: Fills or replaces a selected area from a text prompt, or from the surrounding pixels when the prompt is empty. A model picker lists Adobe Firefly models and partner models; results come as variations in the Properties panel.

Colour management converts between device-dependent spaces (RGB, CMYK) and device-independent models using profiles. Photoshop embeds profiles, converts documents to another profile, sets policy on opening, and supports soft proofing.
The Character panel exposes OpenType features of a font: standard and discretionary ligatures, contextual alternates, swash, old-style figures and others. Applies to selected text or to new text.
Export As saves layers, groups or artboards as PNG, JPG, GIF or SVG with format settings, and can write several relative sizes (for example 1.25x) with a filename suffix in one step.
capabilities.inputs: layers, groups or artboards, scale list

capabilities.does: Runs JavaScript (.js, .jsx), plus VBScript on Windows and AppleScript on macOS. A Script Events Manager runs a script or action on events such as open, save or export. UXP is the framework for new scripts.

Photoshop plugins run on UXP, which has its own JavaScript engine and a curated set of UI components. The UXP API covers files, UI and network I/O; the Photoshop DOM API reaches the document. A UXP Developer Tool creates, debugs and packages plugins.
capabilities.outputs: panel or command in the app

capabilities.does: Actions record a sequence of commands for replay. The contents index lists batch processing, droplets (actions packaged as drag-and-drop files), an Image Processor and conditional actions.
Documents can hold several artboards for multi-screen layouts, and shapes or text can be converted into frames that crop a placed image.
Type can follow a path or fill a shape, be warped, converted to shapes or work paths, and used to create selection borders.
Supports frame-based animation and a timeline with keyframed layer properties, video layers, and export to video or image sequences.

outcomes: web and social images at several scales

rea.notes: Pages on helpx.adobe.com refused automated fetch (HTTP 403); read through a browser tab. The new desktop manual is short per page: parameter detail is thinner than the older manual.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, manual pages read in browser (blend modes, layer styles, adjustments, smart objects, masks, brush dynamics, content-aware fill, liquify, pen, crop, neural filters, generative fill, export as, scripts); four capabilities taken from the manual contents index only

entries.name: Adobe Illustrator

engines.name: Image Trace
engines.does: Converts a raster image into vector paths using presets and tunable colour, path, corner and noise settings.

engines.name: Pathfinder and Shape Builder
engines.does: Two boolean-geometry systems: panel operations on overlapping shapes, and an interactive tool that merges or erases regions.

engines.name: Appearance stack (fills, strokes, effects)
engines.does: Each object carries an ordered list of fills, strokes and effects that can be saved as graphic styles.

engines.name: Generative vector tools (Firefly)
engines.does: Text-prompt and image-based generation of vector artwork, patterns and recolouring.

capabilities.does: Pathfinder panel offers Unite, Minus Front, Intersect, Exclude, Divide, Trim, Merge, Crop, Outline and Minus Back on overlapping shapes. Options set precision and removal of redundant points; results can be kept as a live compound shape.

The Shape Builder tool merges regions by dragging across them, or erases edges and regions while Alt/Option is held. Gap detection takes small (3 pt), medium (6 pt), large (12 pt) or a custom length to close open outlines.

Path creation uses the Pen, Curvature and Pencil tools, with Smooth and Eraser tools for refinement. The manual covers joining open paths, simplifying paths automatically or by hand, and cutting paths.
Simplify reduces anchor points on a path while keeping its shape, either automatically or with a slider and advanced options. The Smooth tool and a smoothness slider reduce wobble in drawn segments.
The Width tool varies stroke thickness along a path by dragging points on the stroke, including pointed ends. Widths can be saved as stroke profiles and applied from a profile menu.
The Stroke panel sets weight, alignment (center, inside, outside for closed paths), butt, round or projecting caps, miter, round or bevel joins, and a miter limit from 1 to 500 with default 10.

Image Trace turns a raster into vector shapes. Presets: auto-colour, high colour, low colour, greyscale, black and white, outline. Settings: colour mode and palette, path fit, corner emphasis, noise area, abutting or overlapping method, fills or strokes.
Three gradient types: linear, radial and freeform (points or lines mode). Linear and radial work on fills and strokes with an on-object annotator for angle, spread and stops; freeform fills only.

Mesh objects hold colour at mesh points set on crossing mesh lines; the area between four points is a patch. Points behave like anchors and accept colour, so colour flows in several directions. A gradient fill can be converted to a mesh.
Blend creates intermediate objects between two shapes. Spacing is smooth colour, a specified number of steps, or a specified distance; orientation aligns to page or to path.
capabilities.inputs: two or more objects, spacing mode

capabilities.does: Symbols are reusable artwork with instances linked to a master. The panel can redefine a symbol across instances, replace, duplicate, break the link, reset instance transforms, select all instances or all unused symbols, and set static or dynamic type.

Object > Repeat makes live grid, radial or mirror repeats of artwork. Grid options include horizontal and vertical spacing, grid type, and row or column flipping, plus on-canvas handles to add rows and columns.

The Recolor dialog remaps the colours of selected artwork using a colour library, a limit on colour count, a theme picker, a colour wheel with linked harmony handles, prominent-colour weights and random shuffles; results save as a swatch group.

The OpenType panel toggles standard and discretionary ligatures, contextual alternates, swash, stylistic and titling alternates, figure styles, position, ordinals, fractions and stylistic sets, where the font supports them.
Variable fonts can be filtered in the font menu by technology. The Character panel then shows sliders for axes such as weight, width and slant.

Area type, text threads between frames, text wrap around objects, rows and columns, margins and first-baseline settings are supported. The index also lists Kashida and hyphenation justification, plus Mojikumi and Kinsoku rules for Japanese.
Type can be set on an open or closed path, flipped, moved along it, spaced and given effects.

Envelope Distort bends artwork to a shape or mesh. Options: anti-alias for raster, preserve shape through clipping mask or transparency, fidelity percent, and whether appearance, linear gradients and pattern fills distort too.
Clipping masks hide parts of objects outside a mask shape; opacity masks use a greyscale object to set transparency and can be inverted or clipped. Both can be released or deactivated.
Objects, groups and layers carry opacity and blending modes. The manual has a page on blending-mode types and a preview of transparency flattening for print or export.
Appearance attributes allow several fills, strokes and effects per object, kept in an ordered stack. Graphic styles store a whole appearance for reuse, with style libraries.
Live Paint groups treat overlapping paths as faces and edges that can be coloured separately with a bucket tool; a gap-finding option closes small openings.
capabilities.outputs: regions coloured as a flat map

capabilities.does: A perspective grid lets artwork be drawn and moved on grid planes. Vanishing points, grid cell size and extent, horizon heights and planes are adjustable, and grid presets can be saved.
A 3D and Materials panel creates 3D objects and text, rotates them, maps artwork onto surfaces, adds custom bevel paths, renders the result and exports 3D vector artwork.
Documents hold many artboards that can be added, duplicated, resized, reordered, aligned, locked and given background colours; artwork can scale with the artboard.
Export for Screens exports artboards, or assets collected for export, in several formats and scales at once: PNG, JPEG, SVG, PDF, WebP, AI, EPS or TIFF, to a folder or to cloud storage.
capabilities.inputs: artboards or assets, format and scale list
capabilities.outputs: image and vector files per size

capabilities.does: Save Adobe PDF offers PDF/X-1a, X-3 and X-4 standards and compatibility levels. X-4 keeps live transparency. An option embeds full Illustrator data so the PDF stays editable.
SVG is an export target in Export for Screens.
Colour modes can be converted, spot colours defined by Lab values, colour separations previewed, traps added between objects, and prints made with colour management.
Scripts run from File > Scripts and can be written in JavaScript or ExtendScript (.jsx), Visual Basic or AppleScript. Sample scripts ship with the app; custom ones are placed in the Scripting folder.
A Variables panel and dynamic objects let artwork be driven by variables, so one template can produce many data-driven variants.
Built-in graph objects can change graph type, combine different graph types and format graph text.
Generative features produce vector patterns, recolouring from text prompts, expanded artwork, and vector artwork from raster images, with similar-variation generation.

rea.notes: Manual pages on helpx.adobe.com refused automated fetch (HTTP 403); read via a browser tab. Several capabilities are cited to the manual contents index, which lists page titles only.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, manual pages read in browser (Pathfinder, Shape Builder, Image Trace, gradients, mesh, blend options, strokes, symbols, repeat, recolor, OpenType, variable fonts, envelope, Export for Screens, PDF/X, scripts, Width tool); about a third from the contents index

entries.name: Figma (Design, FigJam, Dev Mode)

licence.name: Free starter plan; paid Professional, Organization and Enterprise seats

engines.name: Auto layout
engines.does: Rule-based container layout: flow direction, gap, padding, alignment, hug or fill sizing, min and max limits, wrap, and a grid flow.

engines.name: Variables (collections and modes)
engines.does: Typed values (colour, number, string, boolean, timing, easing) grouped in collections and switched by modes such as light and dark.

engines.name: Prototype engine with Smart Animate
engines.does: Interaction graph of triggers and actions between frames, with name-and-hierarchy matching to animate differences between frames.

engines.name: Dev Mode and Code Connect
engines.does: Read-focused workspace that shows specs, generated code and, through Code Connect, the real component code of a design system.

capabilities.does: Frames arrange children vertically, horizontally or in a grid, with wrap, padding (uniform, per axis or per side), gap (number or auto: between, around, evenly), alignment incl. baseline, and per-child hug, fill, fixed, min and max sizes. Children can opt out of the flow.
capabilities.outputs: responsive container that resizes with content

capabilities.does: Constraints pin a layer inside a frame: left, right, left and right, center or scale horizontally; top, bottom, top and bottom, center or scale vertically. The layer then follows the parent as it resizes.
capabilities.outputs: layer that repositions or stretches on resize

capabilities.does: Components are reusable masters with instances. Component properties are boolean (layer visibility), instance swap with preferred instances, text, variant (a set of variations such as state or size) and slot (a flexible area inside an instance).

Variables hold colour, number, string, boolean, timing and easing values in collections of up to 5,000. Modes give each variable one value per context, such as light and dark. They bind to fills, strokes, radius, spacing, type, visibility and more.

Each interaction pairs a trigger with an action. Triggers: on click or tap, on drag, while hovering, while pressing, keyboard or gamepad, mouse enter, leave, down and up, after delay, when video hits a time, when video ends.

Smart Animate matches layers between two frames by name and hierarchy position and animates scale, position, opacity, rotation and fill changes, with easing and duration. Drop and inner shadows and shape-to-shape moves fall back to a dissolve.

Four non-destructive boolean operations on selected shapes: union, subtract, intersect and exclude. The group stays editable for size, position and radius and can be ungrouped. Flatten merges the result into one path.
Shape builder, entered from vector edit mode, merges regions by dragging, extracts a region into its own layer by clicking, and removes a region with Alt/Option-click. The changes are destructive.

Shape tools: rectangle with corner radius, line and arrow with caps and dashes, ellipse, polygon, star (count 3 to 60, ratio, radius) and an arc tool for pies, rings and donuts. The pen builds vector networks.

A Variable tab in type settings gives sliders or input boxes for each font axis such as weight, width, optical size, italic and slant; hovering previews an axis. Frequent axis settings appear in the font style menu.

Type settings expose OpenType features by font (for Inter: letter forms, stylistic sets, character variants, horizontal spacing, fractions), alongside line height, letter spacing, paragraph spacing and indent, list styles, text case, truncation with max lines and underline options.

Each selection can hold several export settings. Formats PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF. Scale accepts a multiplier (x), fixed width (w) or fixed height (h); a suffix is added to filenames. Colour profile choices: same as file, sRGB, Display P3.
capabilities.inputs: layers, frames or page; export settings

capabilities.does: SVG export has switches to outline text, include an id attribute and simplify strokes. Without outlining, text stays editable in the SVG.

Dev Mode adds an inspect panel, code snippets in chosen languages and units, compare-changes view, measurements, annotations, asset export, a ready-for-dev list and focus view, dev resource links, and a VS Code extension.
capabilities.outputs: specs, code and assets for developers

capabilities.does: Code Connect links design-system components to repository components. A UI method (language-agnostic, GitHub link or manual paths) and a CLI method (templates for property mappings, real code snippets in Dev Mode) exist. Examples named: React, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, Vue.
capabilities.outputs: real code shown next to designs and passed to AI agents

capabilities.does: Plugins run inside Figma or FigJam with an open file, using the global figma object and typed node classes; each needs a manifest.json and typings are published on npm. A separate Widget API creates interactive on-canvas nodes.

The REST API at api.figma.com reads files, images, versions, comments, projects, components, styles, variables, dev resources and webhooks, authenticating with access tokens or OAuth2. An OpenAPI spec is published openly.
capabilities.outputs: JSON file data and rendered images

capabilities.does: FigJam is a board with sticky notes, shapes, connectors and lines, sections, stamps, voting sessions, templates and widgets.
FigJam connectors and lines link shapes and stickies into flowcharts and maps; sections group parts of a board.
The Design tab carries blend modes per layer, together with fill, stroke and effects groups. The page names the groups but not each mode.

Set variable and Conditional actions use expressions: arithmetic on numbers, string joining, boolean comparison and logic (==, !=, and, or, >, <, >=, <=, not), with the usual order of operations. They drive carts, counters and checklists in prototypes.
Styles store combined values at once (gradients, blend modes, images, video); variables store single raw values that change with the active mode.

Animations made in Figma Motion export from top-level frames as MP4, WebM, GIF or SVG with size, frame rate, quality and loop settings, or as Lottie JSON and dotLottie. Lottie lacks shader, video and angular-gradient support. Open beta.

rea.notes: Editor is closed. REST API is described by a public OpenAPI spec and the plugin API ships public typings. Help pages were read through WebFetch.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, help-centre and developer pages fetched (auto layout, constraints, components, variables, triggers, Smart Animate, booleans, shape builder, shapes, variable fonts, export, Dev Mode, Plugin and REST API, FigJam); all items from pages opened

entries.name: Inkscape

engines.name: Live Path Effects
engines.does: Non-destructive, parameterised path modifiers (bend, power stroke, pattern along path, tiling, roughen and others) stored on the object.

engines.name: SVG filter system with Filter Editor and Filter Gallery
engines.does: Applies and edits SVG filter chains on objects; it includes a gallery of premade filters with previews.

engines.name: Extensions (Python)
engines.does: Add-on commands in the Extensions menu, written in Python, for generating, arranging and exporting artwork.

capabilities.does: Eight path operations: Union, Difference, Intersection, Exclusion (odd coverage), Division (lower path cut by upper), Cut Path (split at intersections), Combine (one object, all parts) and Break Apart (one object per subpath).
The Node tool inserts, deletes, joins, merges and breaks nodes and path segments, and converts nodes between cusp, smooth, symmetric and auto-smooth types.

The Pen tool has Bezier, Spiro, BSpline, straight-line and paraxial modes. A click adds a node, a short drag pulls out a handle, right-click ends the path. The Pencil tool has Bezier, Spiro and BSpline modes with a smoothing value and an interactive simplify step.

Pencil shape options give a stroke a profile: triangle in or out, ellipse (tapered ends), a shape copied from the clipboard used as a brush, a line bent along a copied curve, the last applied shape, or none for constant width.

The Gradient tool drags a linear gradient onto an object: a square handle marks the start, a round one the end; double-click the line to add stops, then recolour in Fill and Stroke. A button switches to radial. Fill and stroke can have separate gradients.
Preset patterns apply from the Fill and Stroke dialog to fills or strokes, with immediate effect.

The Tweak tool edits many objects with a brush circle of set width and force (pressure sensitivity optional). Modes: move, shrink or grow objects, rotate, duplicate, push path parts, shrink or grow path parts, roughen, paint colour, jitter colours, blur.

Fifteen documented effects, among them Bend, Corners (fillet or chamfer), Hatches, Interpolate and Stitch Sub-Paths, Knot, Mirror Symmetry, Perspective/Envelope, Pattern Along Path, Offset, Power Stroke, Rotate Copies, Roughen, Sketch and Tiling.
The Power Stroke effect adds on-canvas handles that vary the width of a path along its length.
The Calligraphy tool paints variable-width strokes controlled by width, thinning, angle, fixation, caps, tremor, wiggle, mass and pen pressure; a profile can be saved and loaded.

Trace Bitmap has single-scan modes (brightness cutoff, edge detection, colour quantization, autotrace, centerline tracing for line art) and multiple scans that create one stacked object per scan, with live preview via Update.

The Mesh Gradient tool creates a grid with chosen rows and columns on an object; each node carries its own colour, handles reshape patches, and meshes can be reused through the Fill and Stroke dialog.
capabilities.inputs: object, rows and columns, node colours

capabilities.does: A clone (Alt+D) is a linked copy that follows the original shape and style while allowing its own size and rotation. It can be unlinked to become editable, and the original can be selected from the clone.

The Filters menu applies SVG filter combinations to selected objects; a Filter Editor edits their components and a Filter Gallery lists premade filters with previews. Drop shadow offers outer, inner, outer cutout, inner cutout and shadow-only types.
Object > Clip > Set hides everything outside the top shape. Object > Mask > Set uses colour of the top object: darker areas hide more, and a white mask acts like a clip.
The Stroke Style tab sets width, join shape, end caps and dash pattern with offset. A stroke can be painted with flat colour, gradient, pattern or mesh gradient.
Markers can be placed on path ends and nodes, ordered relative to stroke and fill, and custom markers can be built from drawings.
capabilities.outputs: path with arrowheads or node symbols

capabilities.does: Plain canvas text (not frame-flowed) is joined to a path: select both with the Selector tool, then run Text > Put on Path. The path becomes the baseline and later path edits reshape the text. Vertical kerning moves the text off the baseline.

An SVG Font Editor builds fonts on a typography template: add one glyph per layer with a matching string, draw each as a closed path, take curves from the selection. The font stays inside the SVG; converting it needs FontForge.

The text toolbar offers font family and style, size, line height, alignment, sub and superscript, letter, word and kerning spacing, vertical and right-to-left orientation, and a Variants tab for OpenType features such as ligatures.
The Export PNG dialog exports the Page, the whole Drawing, the Selection or a Custom area, with image size set in pixels or resolution.
PDF export can embed fonts, convert text to paths or omit text with a LaTeX file, rasterise filter effects at a chosen dpi, add a bleed margin and choose page or drawing area.
Native format is SVG. Export choices include optimised SVG, plain SVG without editor data, PDF, EPS, PS, EMF, WMF, XAML, DXF and HPGL for plotters.
Imports Illustrator AI (9.0 and newer), CorelDRAW CDR 7 to X4 and CDT templates, Visio VSD, VSDX and VDX, XAML, DXF R13, WMF and EMF, EPS, PostScript and PDF, sometimes only a subset of features.
Release 1.4 adds import of Affinity Designer files and support for internal links in exported PDF files.

Extensions are Python add-ons listed in menus such as Arrange, Color, Export, Generate from Path, Render, Text, Typography and Gcodetools; examples are Interpolate, Pattern along Path, Barcode, Printing Marks and Lorem Ipsum.

rea.notes: Repository page names a LICENSE link to COPYING without stating the licence on the page; GPL-3.0-or-later comes from the Wikipedia comparison, and the site footer says GPL. Latest release seen: 1.4.4 (site banner). Manual used is the Beginners' Guide for 1.3; some options may differ in 1.4.

entries.name: Skia

capabilities.does: A 2D drawing library for text, geometry and images, used as the graphics engine in Chrome, ChromeOS, Android and Flutter. One API targets many hardware and software platforms.
capabilities.inputs: draw calls: paths, text, images, paints

capabilities.does: Backends listed for Skia: CPU software rasterisation, GPU through ANGLE, Vulkan and Metal, and document outputs for PDF, SVG and XPS.

rea.notes: Repository description: a complete 2D graphics library for text, geometries and images. Licence read on the GitHub page.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, skia.org and GitHub page fetched; backend list from the Wikipedia article

capabilities.does: Skia compiled to WebAssembly and drawn to an HTML canvas through WebGL. It exposes the Skia canvas, paint, path and text APIs with TypeScript definitions in the canvaskit-wasm npm package.
SkParagraph provides multi-line paragraph layout and shaping in the browser. Custom shaders and perspective transforms are also exposed.
Skottie plays Lottie animations inside CanvasKit.

rea.notes: Licence taken from the Skia repository page.

entries.name: cairo

capabilities.does: C library with a PostScript and PDF-like drawing model: fill and stroke cubic Bezier paths, composite translucent images, draw anti-aliased text, and apply any affine transform.
The same drawing code can target X11 windows, Quartz, Win32, image buffers, PostScript, PDF and SVG surfaces with consistent output.
capabilities.outputs: screen, bitmap, PS, PDF or SVG

outcomes: vector rendering for GTK apps and SVG renderers

Shaping goes through HarfBuzz. Font maps, families, faces and font descriptions select fonts; backends exist for Cairo, FreeType and Fontconfig.
A markup parser turns tagged text into plain text plus attributes such as weight or colour.

outcomes: text rendering in GTK apps, Inkscape and GIMP

capabilities.does: Configurable diagramming and whiteboarding app written in JavaScript, run in a browser, as a desktop app, as a Docker image or a .war package. Real-time collaboration is not part of this repository.

The README says draw.io is not an SVG editor: its SVG output exists to put diagrams on web pages, not to be edited in other tools. It also says the project claims no copyright over diagrams that users make.

rea.restrictions: README: stencil libraries, icon sets and templates may not be used in or shipped with Atlassian products without written permission.
rea.notes: Pull requests are not accepted per the README.

capabilities.does: Infinite canvas whiteboard with a hand-drawn look, dark mode, image support and shape libraries; exports PNG, SVG or clipboard; drawings save as open .excalidraw JSON. An npm React component embeds the editor.
The hosted app adds real-time collaboration with end-to-end encryption, local autosave, read-only share links and offline PWA use.

engines.name: Typst layout engine
engines.does: Lays out content into pages with flow, grid, stack, columns, placement and transform primitives.

capabilities.does: Markup-based typesetting system with a scripting language, compiler and web app. Exports PDF, HTML, PNG and SVG. Reference covers syntax, styling, scripting, context, math and layout.
Layout elements: page, pagebreak, grid, stack, columns, colbreak, block, box, align, pad, place, h and v spacing, rotate, scale, skew, move, hide, repeat, plus layout and measure for reading sizes.

The text function takes font, fallback, weight, stretch, size, tracking, spacing, lang, region, hyphenate, kerning, ligatures (standard, discretionary, historical), alternates, stylistic-set, number-type, number-width, slashed-zero, fractions, features and variations.

rea.notes: Licence not on pages read. Typst's layout core is covered here rather than as a separate entry. Licence and source availability not confirmed from pages read.

OpenType feature code gets live syntax checking while typing, and feature code can be generated automatically.

Python 3 scripting with the TypeRig library.
Imports PDF, EPS and SVG artwork with autotrace; exports OTF, TTF, WOFF2, WOFF, EOT, UFO, designspace and Glyphs files, colour fonts and batches.

Changes propagate to multiple open windows in real time; collaboration features such as shared selections and comments are listed on the roadmap.
